eras.title: Feudal Roots
eras.summary: The Nizam's autocracy rests on deshmukhs, jagirdars and the vetti system of forced labour. The Andhra Mahasabha begins as a reformist cultural forum.

eras.title: The Sangham Rises
eras.summary: Communists take the lead in the Andhra Mahasabha. Village sanghams fight illegal exactions and evictions; Doddi Komarayya's martyrdom sparks the revolt.

eras.title: Armed Struggle Against the Nizam
eras.summary: The Nizam refuses to join India and unleashes the Razakars. Villages arm themselves, guerrilla squads form, landlords flee, land is redistributed and gram raj spreads to 3,000 villages.

eras.title: 'Police Action'
eras.summary: The Indian Army enters Hyderabad State on 13 September 1948. The Nizam surrenders within five days; the landlords return behind the army.

eras.title: Partisan Resistance Under Terror
eras.summary: To defend the land won, squads fight on from the Godavari and Krishna forests against 50,000 troops: concentration camps, burnt villages, and the killing of captured cadre.

eras.title: Withdrawal & Legacy
eras.summary: The armed struggle is withdrawn on 21 October 1951. The Communists win big in the 1952 elections; Vishalandhra and linguistic states follow.

events.title: Economic crises — landlords grab land
events.desc: In years of bad harvests and price crashes, feudal landlords seize lands left to the peasants in the survey settlement, torturing those unable to pay taxes.

events.title: Majlis Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen formed
events.desc: The Nizam encourages the MIM to rally Muslim masses behind his throne on the plea that 'Muslims are the rulers'.

events.title: Andhra Mahasabha organised
events.desc: Led by Madapati Hanumantha Rao, the Andhra Mahasabha (AMS) begins as a forum for Telugu language, schools and modest reforms.

events.title: First AMS conference at Jogipet
events.desc: Chaired by Suravaram Pratapa Reddy, the first conference passes resolutions for administrative reform and schools.

events.title: Vande Mataram ban sparks student revolt
events.desc: The Nizam bans the singing of Vande Mataram; students backed by democratic forces protest. The State Congress is formed and banned.

events.title: Youth take over the Andhra Mahasabha
events.desc: At the Malkapuram session the youth leadership comes together; Ravi Narayan Reddy becomes President for the Chilukuru conference.

events.title: Ban on the Communist Party lifted
events.desc: Forced by the anti-fascist war, the British lift the ban; Communists work legally and expand among peasants, workers and students.

events.title: Sanghams launch militant struggles
events.desc: Under Communist leadership the AMS fights zamindars and deshmukhs — against vetti, illegal exactions and evictions.

events.title: Bhongir session — the AMS splits
events.desc: At the eleventh session under Ravi Narayan Reddy the right wing walks out. The main body becomes the real leadership of the Telangana people.

events.title: Last AMS session at Khammam
events.desc: The twelfth and final session calls on the people to struggle actively for their demands.

events.title: Ailamma's harvest is defended
events.desc: Visnur Ramachandra Reddy tries to seize the land of Ailamma, a washerwoman and Sangham worker, at Palakurthi. Sangham volunteers drive his goondas away and gather her harvest.

events.label: 4 July 1946
events.title: Doddi Komarayya martyred at Kadavendi
events.desc: The Visnur deshmukh's goondas fire on a Sangham procession. Village leader Doddi Komarayya is killed — the spark that sets the Telangana agrarian revolt afire.

events.label: Nov 1946
events.title: Armed police raid Balemula
events.desc: Police raid villages harbouring Party leaders. Devaruppula, Patasuryapet and Balemula resist; nearly 200 are arrested.

events.label: Jan–Apr 1947
events.title: Regrouping under repression
events.desc: The Party and AMS, under ban and attack, regroup the scattered organisation under heavy blows of the Nizam's repression.

events.label: 15 Aug 1947
events.title: Indian independence — the Nizam refuses to join
events.desc: Power is transferred to the Congress. The Nizam declares he will not join the Indian Union; the struggle for accession merges with the agrarian revolt.

events.title: Razakars let loose on villages
events.desc: Kasim Razvi's Razakar army, backed by the Nizam's forces, loots, burns, tortures and rapes across Telangana.

events.label: Late 1947
events.title: Land distribution sanctioned
events.desc: The insistent demand of the fighting masses wins permission from the Polit Bureau to seize and distribute land.

events.label: 28 Nov 1947
events.title: 6,000 people raid the Kolanupaka camp
events.desc: Villagers gather to raid the jagirdar's Razakar camp in Bhongir taluka.

events.label: 29 Nov 1947
events.title: Three thousand march on Aleru
events.desc: Flag-hoisting marchers are fired on by armed police; the people surge forward regardless.

events.label: Jan 1948
events.title: Gundrampalli Razakar camp raided
events.desc: Squads of Kandada Balireddy and Kodandarama Reddy raid the notorious Razakar camp.

events.label: 30 Jan 1948
events.title: Communist Party banned again
events.desc: After a short period of legality following independence, the Party is banned and attacked once more.

events.label: Apr 1948
events.title: Guerrilla squads and Koya squads formed
events.desc: Six firka squads of 20 each and 40–50 squads of Koya people — about 1,000 fighters — are organised in the Godavari forest area.

events.label: Jun 1948
events.title: 50 shot dead in one month
events.desc: Nizam's forces intensify terror: in June 1948 alone 50 people are shot dead, 38 of them in the Garla area.

events.title: Gram raj in 3,000 villages
events.desc: Village panch committees administer about 3,000 villages: land distribution, education, health and rural services run by the fighting people's committees.

events.title: One million acres distributed
events.desc: Surplus, illegally seized, waste, forest and grazing lands — 10 lakh acres — are distributed with full ownership rights to the rural poor.

events.label: 13 Sep 1948
events.title: Indian Army's 'police action'
events.desc: The Union launches 'police action' on Hyderabad State. Except in a few pockets like Kodada, the Nizam's forces surrender without resistance.

events.label: 18 Sep 1948
events.title: The Nizam surrenders
events.desc: Within five days the Nizam surrenders — and is promised all his privileges and purses.

events.label: Autumn 1948
events.title: Decision to continue the armed struggle
events.desc: To defend the land won from being seized back by landlords returning behind the army, the Party decides to keep up armed resistance.

events.label: Dec 1948
events.title: Military terror reaches full intensity
events.desc: Launched within two weeks of the army's entry, the military terror attack peaks by the end of December 1948.

events.label: Dec 1948
events.title: Hyderabad municipal workers strike
events.desc: 1,600 municipal workers take to the streets with the red flag, demanding a living wage and permanency.

events.label: Jan 1949
events.title: Raids and forced levies in Miryalagudem
events.desc: The enemy intensifies raids and starts collecting grazing fees and land taxes; landlords pressure peasants to pay.

events.label: May 1949
events.title: Textile workers strike again
events.desc: Mill workers strike for bonus, rice rations and restoration of civil liberties; more militants are arrested.

events.title: Terror in the Andhra rear
events.desc: In Andhra more than 1,000 villages are raided, 25,000 people beaten and 10,000 arrested as the Madras government crushes support for Telangana.

events.label: Jul 1949
events.title: 500 landlords and agents killed
events.desc: By July 1949, five hundred landlords and agents have been killed; the rest dare not return and stay in the military camps.

events.label: Oct 1949
events.title: Calculated killing of 300 captured cadre
events.desc: From October 1949 the forces carry out the physical annihilation of about 300 Communist leaders and cadre after arresting them.

events.label: Dec 1949
events.title: Military rule replaced by Vellodi administration
events.desc: Maj-Gen. Chowdhury's military government gives way to a civil administration under M. K. Vellodi.

events.label: Jan 1950
events.title: Squads extend into Devarkonda
events.desc: Squads from the Miryalagudem zone penetrate Devarkonda villages and distribute landlords' grain.

events.label: 26 Jan 1950
events.title: The Nizam becomes Raj Pramukh
events.desc: As the Republic's Constitution comes into force, the Nizam is formally declared Raj Pramukh of Hyderabad State.

events.title: Koya concentration camps — 10,000 dead
events.desc: Koya people are driven from forest hamlets into camps like Gadepadu, where cholera kills about 10,000; 300 more are shot.

events.label: Nov 1950
events.title: November Day & Peace Day
events.desc: Red flags, meetings and demonstrations across the Krishna forest region.

events.label: End 1950
events.title: Delegation meets the international movement
events.desc: A Party delegation meets the CPSU leadership and Stalin to resolve inner-party differences over the path of the Indian revolution.

events.title: Extension to Chennur–Sirpur
events.desc: The movement crosses into the Chennur–Sirpur area of Adilabad district.

events.label: May 1951
events.title: Central Committee reviews Telangana
events.desc: After a thorough discussion of the Telangana situation, the Central Committee adopts its resolution on the way forward.

events.label: Jun 1951
events.title: Leaders go into the forests to explain
events.desc: Leaders travel to the Godavari forest area to meet the guerrillas and explain the new understanding.

events.label: 21 Oct 1951
events.title: Armed struggle withdrawn
events.desc: The guerrillas hear on the radio that the armed struggle has been called off. No amnesty is declared.

events.title: First general elections
events.desc: The Communist Party emerges as the single biggest opposition group in the first Parliament; PDF candidates sweep Telangana.

events.label: Mar 1952
events.title: Cadres reject the 'wrong to continue' view
events.desc: The Central Committee and Telangana cadres conclude it was right to have continued armed defence of the land after 1948.

events.title: Andhra state and linguistic states
events.desc: Telangana inspires the movement that wins the Andhra state after Potti Sreeramulu's martyrdom (1952), paving the way for linguistic states in 1956.

events.label: Dec 1972
events.title: This book is published
events.desc: 'At last, after 20 years' delay', Sundarayya's narrative is placed in readers' hands.

figures.label: land distributed to the rural poor
in detention camps and jails for 3–4 years
10,000 houses destroyed in a single year
owned 60–70% of cultivable land in 3 districts
on police & military in half a year (Godavari)
killed by the people by July 1949

people.name: Doddi Komarayya
people.bio: Sangham leader of Kadavendi, shot dead leading a procession on 4 July 1946 — the first martyr of the revolt.

people.name: Chakali Ailamma
people.bio: Washerwoman and Sangham worker of Palakurthi whose harvest the Sangham defended against the Visnur deshmukh.

people.name: Ravi Narayan Reddy
people.bio: AMS President, Communist leader of Telangana; later argued for withdrawal after the police action.

people.name: Baddam Yella Reddy
people.bio: AMS leader who, with Ravi Narayan Reddy, brought the organisation to the Communist Party.

people.name: Suravaram Pratapa Reddy
people.bio: Chaired the first AMS conference at Jogipet, 1930.

people.name: Bandagi
people.bio: Peasant martyred fighting the Visunur deshmukh in the 1920s; immortalised in the play Ma Bhoomi.

people.name: Swarajyam
people.bio: Active since 1945 as a young girl in the AMS; a leading woman fighter.

people.name: B. Narasimha Reddy
people.bio: Leader who went to the forests in 1951 to explain the new Central Committee line.

people.name: Comrade John
people.bio: Zonal commander from an agricultural-labour family of Jajireddigudem, Suryapet.

people.name: Renigunta Rami Reddy
people.bio: Bhongir squad leader martyred with his squad of 20 at Aleru.

people.name: P. Sundarayya
people.bio: Author of this book; Communist leader who was in the thick of the struggle.

people.name: Visnur Ramachandra Reddy
people.bio: The hated deshmukh of Jangaon taluka whose goondas killed Doddi Komarayya.

people.name: Kasim Razvi
people.bio: Leader of the Majlis Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen who organised the Razakar army.

people.name: The Nizam
people.bio: Mir Osman Ali Khan, feudal autocrat of Hyderabad State; surrendered 18 Sept 1948, later Raj Pramukh.

people.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
people.bio: Prime Minister whose government sent the army and continued the terror regime.

people.name: Vallabhbhai Patel
people.bio: Home Minister who brought the princely states into the Union, guaranteeing their privileges.

people.name: Maj-Gen. J. N. Chowdhury
people.bio: Military governor of Hyderabad after the police action.

people.name: M. K. Vellodi
people.bio: Head of the civil administration that replaced military rule.

Loved immensely by the labouring people, he was in the forefront of many attacks on the enemies in the whole centre. In 1950, he was passing through Yatavakilla where the police caught

sketches.name: Comrades Balija Ramulu and Chakali Somulu
sketches.text: Both hailed from Chintagunta. Comrade Ramulu was the organiser of the Penchikaladinne centre. He took a leading part in actions to liquidate the hated landlords and police agents, apart from leading agricultural labour and land struggles. In March 1950, he was decoyed by the landlords of Chintagunta, led by Yangala Narsi Reddi, to settle the land problems, p

sketches.name: Comrade Bareddi Saidulu (Reddy)
sketches.text: Squad leader from the Razakar days. Coming from Mellacheruvu he became a centre organiser and fought against Kandibandla Janaki Rama Rao, the notorious landlord. He led many an agricultural labour strike, confiscated enemy property and his cotton carts. Once, after accompanying the zonal organiser to his village, he was waiting in a field when he was spotted

sketches.name: Comrade Pentayya (Koppulu Penta Reddy)
sketches.text: Coming from Amaravaram village, Lingagiri enclave, he was active in agricultural labour strikes. He was very badly beaten in the police camp at the instance of the village munsiff (patel). After his release, he joined the Party in 1950. Immediately afterwards, he liquidated the hated village munsiff. He became an active squad member, and participated in many

sketches.name: Comrade Nasarayya
sketches.text: Belonging to Mellacheruvu, he was a guerrilla squad member, illiterate but determined and brave. He participated in many raids on the police camps and on enemy agents, from the Razakar days. He participated in the raid on the police station in Penuganachiprolu, playing a prominent part. The raiding party, after capturing nearly 20 weapons, retreated and was

sketches.name: Comrade Vakkantu Suryanarayana
sketches.text: Comrade Suryanarayana and four other comrades were shot dead at Keetavarigudem. Suryanarayana belonged to Velidanda village; Harijan Chandrayya to Gondrela, Mera Janayya and Harijan Somayya to Sandrupatla and Chelasani Velama Somayya to Malkapuram. Four of them had joined the squad only in 1950. Comrade Suryanarayana had given up his studies and joined the m

sketches.name: Comrade “Russia” Lingulu
sketches.text: Born in Chintakallu, of Huzurnagar taluka, Comrade Lingulu joined the guerrilla squads against the Razakars and the Nizam. He was an expert, rapid shot, even with his muzzle-loader. After the ‘police action’, when the Party organisation was disrupted due to incessant raids, and the leaders were forced to leave the area, he lived among the people, gave them c

sketches.name: Comrade Ravipati Lingayya
sketches.text: A 60-year-old courier, and expert swimmer, he was in charge of ferrying comrades across the River Krishna, all through the period beginning from the Nizam-Razakar days. He used to gather information from people all around. The police did not get hold of him in spite of their repeated efforts. He trained and recruited his two sons also, for membership into th

sketches.name: Comrade Ramu (Gangiereddi Koti Reddy)
sketches.text: An important cadre in Huzurnagar area, belonging to Timmalagiri-Miryalagudem. He knew the dens of the leading cadre where Rs. 50,000 and four candies (about a ton) of gunpowder and 15 firearms were being kept. He was tortured for 15 days but he did not reveal any information. He died a great martyr’s death.

sketches.name: Comrades Akkala Saidayya and Ginjaluri Pitchayya
sketches.text: Comrade Saidayya came from Bottalapalem village and was working in the Huzurnagar area committee technical apparatus from the Nizam-Razakar days. He knew the ins and outs of the whole forest. He was a great prop to the poor against the forest contractors and guards. Ginjaluri Pitchayya hailed from Jagannathapuram village of Munagala pargana. He led many agri

sketches.name: Comrade Gunda Venkanna
sketches.text: Merchant and well-to-do peasant belonging to Tadakamallu. He joined the Party during the Nalgonda people’s movement, during the Nizam days itself. He developed into a centre organiser after conducting many struggles against the landlord and organised the distribution of thousands of acres of land in the Topucherla centre. He took shelter in Union territory a

sketches.name: Comrade Ranga Reddy
sketches.text: Coming from a rich peasant family of Comareddigudem, he joined the Party during the Nizam days. Active in the land distribution movement especially the lands of the Babasahebpet Deshmukhs, he conducted agricultural labour struggles during 1949, after the ‘police action’, in this centre. Caught by the enemy in January 1950, he was shot dead.

sketches.name: Comrade Appi Reddy
sketches.text: Of Ramadugu centre. A middle peasant, he joined the squad during the Nizam-Razakar days. He was arrested after the ‘police action’ and participated in many struggles in jails. After release in 1950, he rejoined the squads and participated effectively in the raids on buses. His squad was surrounded once and he was arrested. Tortured in Borrayapalem camp, he d

sketches.name: Comrade Akarapu Saidulu
sketches.text: Of Bottalapalem. A farm servant himself, he was a militant leader of agricultural labour strikes. He was many a time caught and tortured by the police and landlords and was caught and shot dead in 1950.

sketches.name: Comrade Sunkara Venkatappayya
sketches.text: Of Ramasamudram village. Squad commander of Munagala, he led many actions and liquidated a number of enemies. One day he was sleeping in a field when the informers brought the police and surrounded him. He fought with his “guider” till the end and after his bullets were exhausted, he and his two companions were overpowered and shot dead.

sketches.name: Comrades Golla Muthayya, Nadayya, Gurram Narsi Reddy
sketches.text: Hailing from the village of Jagannathpuram, Comrade Muthayya was the organiser of the Munagala pargana centre, and from the time he gave up studies, had been in the forefront of the struggle against the Munagala zamindar. He, along with Comrade Nadayya, also from the same village, and with zonal organiser, Comrade Gurram Narsi Reddy, was caught in a secret s

sketches.name: Comrade S. Punnayya
sketches.text: Comrade Punnayya was an agricultural labourer from Anjalipuram village, Munagala pargana, and much respected by the lambadi tanda people. A member of Ramanarsa Reddy’s squad he was caught in Anjalipuram, whilst trying to make Party contacts after the massive raids of 1949-50. He was tortured and shot.

sketches.name: Comrades Gundu Ramulu and Balayya
sketches.text: Comrade Ramulu had participated in many peasant struggles of Munagala and later joined the Telangana people’s struggle. He constantly strove to improve his political and organisational capacities and overcame some of his bad habits. Later, he developed the people’s movement in the Lingala area, in Mehboobnagar district, adjoining the Krishna River valley and

sketches.name: Comrade Uttarayya (Narasimhalu)
sketches.text: Coming from Bollepalli village, Comrade Narasimhalu was working as a clerk under the village landlords. Later, he joined the Party and worked in the guerrilla squads. He was caught with the help of one Sale Ramaswami, a relative of Uttarayya, in Surepalli village and shot dead in the Nandanam military camp.

sketches.name: Comrade Chada Komarayya
sketches.text: Also a clerk, his brother sided with the enemy in the Puligilla struggle and was killed by the guerrillas. At first, he and his second elder brother, Aillayya, were against the Party. But gradually, they understood its ideals and activities, and joined the Party.

sketches.name: Comrade Baddam Narayana
sketches.text: An agricultural labourer, Comrade Narayana led many strikes and won for the labourers monthly wages of 80 seers of paddy. Later he became a wholetime functionary of the Party. When he was forced to go away from West Bhuvanagiri, he joined the railways as a worker. There he was betrayed and shot dead.

sketches.name: Comrade Gokula Mattayya (Reddy)
sketches.text: Comrade Mattayya was arrested during the Nizam period, kept in jail and later let off. Immediately, he, along with his wife, joined the Party, and resumed his activities. Again he was arrested and shot dead, and his wife raped to death.

sketches.name: Comrade Appajipeta Lingayya
sketches.text: Appajipeta Lingayya of Koppolu village, Nalgonda taluka, and Comrade Venkatanaraayya, handloom weaver of Peda village, Ramannapeta taluka, were betrayed in Rapolu village by Home Guards. They were shot dead. Later the Home Guards were severely beaten up by the squads and the main culprits killed.

sketches.name: Comrades Gutta Seeta Rami Reddy and Paila Ramachandra Reddy
sketches.text: The Party had conducted a one-week school in the Rachakonda hillocks. The fifty organisers and squad members were to leave for their respective areas the following morning. One among those who supplied their food that day, betrayed the comrades, and by early morning, a large contingent of the army surrounded the hillock and scoured the area till evening. Nor

sketches.name: Comrade Mukundam
sketches.text: Squad commander Comrade Mukundam went to Hyderabad on some party work. This news somehow reached the army and they arrested him. After torturing him he was taken round various military camps in Ramannapet taluka. Having failed in their mission to extract secrets from him, they took him to Veldevi village (Ramannapet taluka) where they mobilised the people in

sketches.name: Comrade Erra Narsi Reddy
sketches.text: Seven members, of whom one was an organiser and another a courier, gathered at Patelgudem well (Bhongir taluka). Some people also came there to get some of their problems settled. It was about 5 in the morning. This news reached the military and they came with a big force from the Aler and Jangaon camps and encircled the area. The sentry found this out and a

glossary.def: Forced, unpaid labour that every lower-caste family owed the landlord and officials — one of the most hated features of Nizam feudalism.
Hereditary revenue-collecting landlord; the de-facto ruler of a group of villages.
Holder of a jagir — land granted by the Nizam with rights to collect revenue. Jagirs covered about 30% of the state.
'Lord' — how peasants had to address the landlord.
The fortress-like house of a deshmukh or landlord.
Village headman and village accountant — the lowest rung of the Nizam's revenue machinery.
Volunteer militia of the Majlis Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen under Kasim Razvi, used to terrorise villages in 1947–48.
The village-level Andhra Mahasabha association; for peasants simply 'the Sangham'.
The Telugu people's organisation in Hyderabad State (1928), led by Communists from 1944.
Village self-rule through elected people's committees that replaced the landlords' authority.
A guerrilla squad. Village squads, firka squads and regular (district) squads made up the people's forces.
Revenue sub-division of a taluka; used as the unit for guerrilla squads.
Administrative sub-division of a district.
A revenue division or enclave (e.g. Munagala Pargana).
Adivasi people of the Godavari forests who became the backbone of the forest guerrilla zones.
Banjara community; strong supporters of the movement in the Krishna (Nallamala) forest region.
Forest people of the Nallamala hills along the Krishna river.
The government's name for the Indian Army's invasion of Hyderabad State on 13 Sept 1948 ('Operation Polo').
One hundred thousand (10 lakh = 1 million).
Lands illegally seized by landlords from peasants.
Government/common land: grazing grounds, tank beds, etc.
Holder of a makta — a revenue-free grant of a village.
Hired thug of the landlord.
'Greater Andhra' — the demand to unite all Telugu-speaking areas into one state.
